prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1147; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed collision in the parking lot of a grocery store while backing out of a space. Claimant states the other vehicle struck the rear passenger side. Claimant has no lawyer and is handling the claim personally.

Entry 2: Claimant described the same sequence of events in a recorded call, and the account matches what was given at the scene. Claimant reports a wrist fracture from bracing against the dashboard as the impact occurred. The reported injury fits the kind and force of a collision like this.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and a statement from a witness in the next row both confirm the vehicles came into contact as described. The damage pattern on both vehicles lines up with the reported impact. No earlier damage to the claimant's vehicle appears in our records or in the photos supplied.

Entry 4: Claimant is still not completely clear on which seat position they were sitting in at impact, and says the memory is hazy. This does not change the overall description of the collision. No prior injury to the same wrist or arm is known from the medical history provided.

Entry 5: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, with follow-up visits extending past the usual recovery window. The treating provider has documented the progression in notes sent to us. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start date.

Entry 6: The driver involved is a household member of the policyholder and is covered under the policy as such. Coverage review is complete for the driver and vehicle. Claim remains open pending the final treatment summary and a repair estimate.
